label: Voice & TTS
note: Narration and character voices. The decisive change in this lane was architectural: both live engines are CLONERS, so a voice became a reference WAV rather than a preset name.

entities.name: Bark / Bark-Voice-Cloning
entities.summary: Pre-July roster TTS. Replaced by hosted voices before any dated bench on this box.

entities.name: Tortoise TTS
entities.summary: In the old roster alongside Bark; no dated decision records why it went.

entities.name: Azure Neural TTS
entities.summary: The hosted narration voice set. Its voice ids (en-GB-RyanNeural and 64 others) outlived it: they are still the keys 65 catalog rows, GUI dropdowns and every archived job state use, now as opaque identifiers.

issues.text: A cloud dependency and a per-character cost on a pipeline that is otherwise local.
The storyteller degradation badge keyed on 'azure-fallback' and would never have fired again after the swap.
azure_integrations.py was deliberately NOT touched — it is blob upload and EventGrid, not TTS.

entities.name: edge-tts
entities.summary: Used with Azure for narration until the Kokoro stopgap and the pause-map assembler landed.

entities.name: Kokoro-82M
entities.summary: The first local-only narration voice and the fastest thing this stack has ever had at ~0.03x real time. Removed from the codebase when the cloners won the bake-off.

issues.text: A preset-voice model: no cloning, so a character's voice could not be a reference recording.
It could degrade to CPU when VRAM was short; its replacements cannot, which is why a VRAM gate had to be built.

entities.name: Fish-Speech S2-Pro
entities.summary: Registered in the roster and removed on 2026-07-15 without ever being used; Kokoro stayed primary.

issues.text: Removed unused — the roster diff and .tts_removal_backups_20260715 are the only record of why it was there.

entities.name: Orpheus-3B
entities.summary: Same as Fish-Speech: registered, never used, removed in the 07-15 cleanup.

entities.name: IndexTTS-2
entities.summary: Won a blind bake-off and became the single TTS entry point for every pipeline. Emotion is inferred from the text itself (use_emo_text), so there is no markup to maintain.

issues.text: Replaced presets with cloning: a voice is now a reference WAV, and _voice_seed_for() maps a legacy voice id to a deterministic seed so the same id sounds the same across chunks, runs and episodes.
It preserves child timbre, which Maya1's voice design could not produce at all.
Speed regression accepted on the operator's call: ~0.03x real time under Kokoro became ~0.83x, so a 10-minute narration went from seconds to 8-10 minutes of GPU time.
19.7 GB of real VRAM, not the 10-12 GB folklore — the emotion LLM, w2v-bert and BigVGAN are all resident. The worker exits 3 below ZYG_INDEXTTS_MIN_VRAM_MB (21000).

That VRAM gate killed a documentary at Stage 4 — a kids song left 18508 MiB free and research, script, tagging and emotion analysis were thrown away because another job held 2.5 GB too much for a moment.
Emits no word timings, so the existing Whisper backfill is still the timing source.
It is now the ONLY working engine: with Chatterbox gone there is no fallback, and a give-up is a failed job.

entities.name: Chatterbox
entities.summary: ~4.1 GB cloner kept as the fallback under the 21 GB VRAM gate, and as an EU AI Act Art.50 watermarking asset. Retired on the operator's call once its venv was gone.

issues.text: It designed Abel's child voice with a DSP transform when Maya1 could not.

Dead since 02:36 on 2026-10-02: the disk sweep deleted its sibling venv, so every 'falling back to Chatterbox' line logged after that actually meant 'giving up' — and it cost an episode. The guard now says whether a fallback can really run.
Retired rather than reinstalled ('current TTS works fine'), which leaves the lane single-engine. install_chatterbox.sh still exists.

entities.name: Maya1
entities.summary: Not a pipeline voice: it DESIGNS reference wavs. The 16-voice seed pool (8m/8f) every legacy voice id maps onto is Maya1 output, which is why the pool carries no consent exposure. Still the designer for creature voices.

issues.text: Could not design a child voice — all 11 candidates came back adult male, so the child path went to Chatterbox + DSP and then to IndexTTS-2.

entities.name: Applio RVC
entities.role: voice conversion to a fixed singer
entities.licence: MIT (+ ToU: must own the audio)
entities.summary: Converts a rendered kids-song vocal to the fixed Warm Control voice. Wired in for adult_male with pinned weights, a per-song ship_check and an unconverted A/B kept on the card.

issues.text: v1 failed one pre-registered criterion (the model was an AVERAGE of its renditions); v2, built by keeping only renditions with TitaNet cosine to the reference above the median, passed all of them.

It was eating the words: unprompted intelligibility 70.7% unconverted → 62.0% converted, worse on 13 of 16 songs, 25 of 216 lines crossed clear→unclear. Now gated — ship_check compares bare-decode clarity before and after, and 9 of 16 real conversions are refused.
Output level drifts −6..+5 dB vs source and some stems come back 441 samples early — both corrected in the wrapper (sung-RMS gain match, envelope xcorr align) rather than in Applio.
Only one real Warm Control take exists to train on (Red Train rt_m01), so the voice model is built from renditions of itself.
Headless Applio never writes assets/config.json, so every end-of-training weight extraction failed with ENOENT while the checkpoints saved fine.

entities.name: DDSP-SVC
entities.summary: Never installed. Its REQUIRED openvpi NSF-HiFiGAN vocoder is non-commercial — the root-licence trap again, after a 09-06 research note had called the project MIT.

issues.text: Required vocoder is CC BY-NC-SA. Caught only because licences are read at FILE level, not at the repo root.

entities.name: Voice seed pool
entities.summary: 16 Maya1-designed reference wavs plus a manifest. This is what 'a voice' means in the stack now; drop wavs in and update the manifest to grow it.

issues.text: Synthetic by design, so no consent or likeness exposure — the reason the cloner swap was safe to make.
